coverage_claim: Proposed source-grounded engineering-definition information contract with individually authored questions, typed field groups and qualified design boundaries. It is not exhaustive sector coverage, executable engineering tooling or an independently certified specification.

boundary_decision.rationale: One informational design revision owns coherent intended-definition assertions and baseline bindings. Product family, variant, BOM, physical item, requirement and execution masters remain external. Registry packaging standalone-mm is separate from the research aggregate classification.

decisions.rationale: The frozen result explicitly separates nominal engineering definition from observed location, mass, wear and operating state of an item. The former workstream's physical-subject assumption is not inherited.
REFERENCE to WM-REC-006 preserves design-realizes-requirement traceability. Allocation and scoped satisfaction evidence do not assume ownership of requirement content.

Design identity is independent of filenames and exports. Competing drawing and model assertions stay contested until the declared design authority resolves them; the latest timestamp does not silently win.
Verification of requirements and validation against stakeholder intent are separately qualified for the design revision. Neither establishes manufactured-item safety or legal certification.
The result distinguishes machine-interpretable feature associations and tolerances from graphical annotations. Matching rendered geometry is insufficient evidence of lossless engineering exchange.
NASA guidance is domain-specific and does not impose a universal baseline workflow. NIST selected historical fixtures do not establish current tool capability or exhaustive real-product conformance.
AP242 is supported only by its public scope. The empty ASME catalogue description is excluded. ReqIF release and selected XSD declarations do not establish a tested semantic mapping.

Nested field descriptions propose an information contract, not an executable instance schema. CAD/PMI adapters, real-product fixtures and calibrated acceptance criteria remain adoption work; no implementation success is claimed.
Expected-base checks, scoped release authority, separate deviation applicability, protected disclosure and retention preserve historical interpretation. A custodian does not become design owner.
Both bounded external research attempts timed out. This audit is a separate frozen-result Codex self-check with no research tools, not an independent reviewer or a Claude/Grok answer.

publication_holds: No independent external research or independent reviewer: Claude and Grok each timed out once at 120 seconds. Source-grounded Codex research and a separate frozen no-tools Codex self-audit are used under owner authorization. This remains reviewable-draft, not canonical.

AP242 licensed clauses and sector-specific engineering/metrology standards were not inspected. ReqIF semantic mapping and source-to-field conformance are untested. No normative standards compliance is claimed.
NIST PMI evidence uses historical selected fixtures and cannot demonstrate current software capability or universal product completeness. NASA process guidance requires local applicability decisions.

No executable instance-validation schema, CAD interpreter, PMI adapter, real design fixture or verified round-trip translator is included. Nested field groups are proposed semantics requiring implementation and tests.

Physical capabilities, tolerances, recognition and safe-use claims require product-specific evidence and qualified engineering review. Information-model validity never authorizes physical action or certification.
The adopting Dimension must instantiate actual design authority, release roles, access controls and retention policy before live engineering records are created or released.
deferred_research: Executable field-level schema and failure fixtures for conflicting authority, stale baseline, unresolved requirement and concurrent change.
Sector-specific engineering geometry, metrology, material, interface and physical-assurance evidence.
Licensed standard inspection and version-specific CAD/PMI/ReqIF crosswalks with explicit unsupported constructs.
Native-versus-derivative real-product tests for geometry, units, tolerances, semantic annotations and requirement traceability.
Independent external research and adversarial review of the completed information contract.
